summary.en: Kuki volunteers were shot dead and other Kuki men were found in gunny bags after attacks by rival groups, prompting rallies demanding the SoO agreement’s abrogation and the return of displaced families. Security forces recovered arms, explosives and Maoist communication equipment from a forest dump in Kanker, while a union minister said the Maoism-free state is becoming a tourism and investment hub. A convoy of the Darbar Move crossed Ramban under tight security and a road accident in Reasi killed one person and injured two. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Kuki-frivillige ble skutt og drept, og andre Kuki-menn ble funnet i gunny-poser etter angrep fra rivaliserende grupper, noe som førte til demonstrasjoner som krever opphevelse av SoO-avtalen og tilbakeføring av fordrevede familier. Sikkerhetsstyrker gjenvant våpen, sprengstoff og maoistisk kommunikasjonsutstyr fra en skogavfallshaug i Kanker, mens en unionsminister sa at den maoistfrie staten blir en turist‑ og investeringshub. En konvoi fra Darbar-bevegelsen krysset Ramban under tett sikkerhet, og en veitrafikkulykke i Reasi drepte én person og såret to. 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
